rationale: Recorded the client-completion result for the re-propose probe and promoted a Fact for the value-adoption line of work, with a new source range for the execution-time reply condition. The re-queue comparison holds, so the replacement decision does not silently consume the client request; the reply side is answered from source and registered as a partially resolved gap because the harness never ran the execution path.

knowledge.statement: Recovery of an instance by a replica that does not hold the instance's command can decide a value different from the value another live replica has already committed for that instance: the fabricated self value ballot lets the recovering coordinator adopt its own empty state, so it re-proposes a NOOP, and that NOOP is then committed at the recovering quorum while the earlier holder keeps its committed command.
knowledge.conditions: N=5, F=2 EPaxos configuration of the captured snapshot with Thrifty on and IsLeader false at the recovering replica; the instance owner fails inside its accept window (after broadcasting Accept or after the first Commit of its broadcast), the recovering replica holds the instance without its command, and the executor retries the recovery (epaxos/epaxos.go:404-417) after the first attempt.

gaps.question: Does the replaced instance itself ever produce a client-visible reply, given that the owner's pending proposals are cleared when the replacement decision arrives?

interpretations.rationale: Current account: the protection around a replacement decision works as the source describes, and the client's request is not silently consumed. Measured in receipt f96da636a32f473280ce82dc0f0a002d (fixed experiment 602b7dcab8064d2ab9113ac315a40743-experiment, test TestAssuranceEPaxosRecoveryReproposesClientRequest, exit 0, 13 parsed events): the owner replica 0 proposed command X with a real GPropose (command id 77, index 1) and its instance held X after its pre-accept reply set (index 2, cmd_op 1); replica 3, which held no command for the instance, recovered it and proposed the NOOP (indices 6 and 7, cmd_op 0) although the owner's own prepare reply carried its command (index 3); the recovered decision reached the live owner, whose instance then held the NOOP (index 9 and index 12, status COMMITTED, cmd_op 0). The declared comparison holds, evaluating index 11: requeued 1, i.e. handleCommit re-queued exactly the pending proposal with command id 77 on the owner's own propose channel and cleared its pending list (pending_proposals 0) - epaxos/epaxos.go:1090-1098. The reply side is answered from source rather than measured: replies are emitted only by the execution path when the executing replica still holds client proposals for the executed instance (epaxos/exec.go:126-138), and the owner's proposals were just cleared, so the replaced instance produces no reply for command 77; the completeness of the client's request therefore rests on the re-proposed request being decided and executed later, which this harness did not run (it reports 0 reply bytes because no executor goroutine exists). No defect is claimed for this relationship: the replacement decision is visibly paired with a re-offer of the client request, at the cost of a fresh instance and a later completion.
counterevidence: The re-propose path is gated on three conditions in handleCommit (owner row, a single NONE command, non-nil pending proposals); a replacement decision carrying a non-NONE command, or an instance owned by a failed replica, leaves the client request un-reproposed, so this protection is narrower than 'every replacement is compensated'.

The measured re-queue happened at the owner because it stayed alive; in the committed-value experiment the owner failed and its request was not re-proposed, which is why that receipt documents the value loss without a compensating path.

The engine's reply condition depends on lb.clientProposals, so the cleared list is what suppresses the reply for the replaced instance; the observation of zero reply bytes is consistent with that but was not produced by an execution path.
limitations: No executor goroutine ran, so the completion of the re-proposed request (a new instance, a new accept/commit cycle, a reply carrying command id 77) is source-derived, not measured.
One command shape (single PUT) and one instance index; the batching case (several commands in one instance) was not exercised, where the re-propose loop pushes every pending proposal.
The re-queued proposal was observed by draining the target's own suggest channel, not through a client connection, and the reply writer was a harness-owned buffer.
interpretations.joint_history: All cited indices belong to receipt f96da636a32f473280ce82dc0f0a002d for fixed experiment 602b7dcab8064d2ab9113ac315a40743-experiment and describe instance (0,0) of one run: index 1 the owner's admitted proposal, indices 2-3 its pre-accept state and the owner's own prepare reply, indices 6-7 the recovery's NOOP proposal, and indices 9-12 the owner's state and re-queue outcome after the replacement decision.
